approach.chosen: Classical Wronskian Sturm comparison + Riccati (log-derivative) comparison with integrating factor + quantitative Euclidean-tangent normalization, all at the scalar ODE level, division-free or with strict-positivity denominators; Bishop-Gromov analytic core as a separate expanded-hypothesis theorem; constant-curvature model j_K reused from the vendored D10 module.
approach.target_statement: Nonconstant scalar Jacobi/Riccati comparison: (A) Sturm zero comparison: k2<=k1 on [a,b], u_i''+k_i u_i=0 on (a,b), u1(a)=u2(a)=0, u2(b)=0, u2>0 on (a,b) ==> u1 has a zero in (a,b) OR k1=k2 on (a,b). (B) Riccati/log-derivative: k2<=k1, u1,u2>0 on [a,b], rho_i=u_i'/u_i, rho1(a)<=rho2(a) ==> rho1<=rho2 on [a,b]; corollary: same value+derivative at a ==> u1<=u2. (C) singular Riccati comparison m' + m^2/d + k <= 0 vs model equality with k>=k_model and |m(t)-d/t|<=C near 0 ==> m<=m_model on (0,T); consequences: A/Abar and V/Vbar antitone (volume-ratio). (D) one-sided Rauch-type corollary u<=j_K for k>=K with u(0)=j_K(0)=0, u'(0)=j_K'(0)=1.
